facts.text: La Mirande sits at the foot of the Palais des Papes in Avignon.
facts.excerpt: La Mirande invites you to enjoy a rare experience of refined hospitality, fine dining, and quiet beauty at the foot of the Palais des Papes.

facts.text: La Mirande is an 18th-century Provencal townhouse.
facts.excerpt: Staying at La Mirande means experiencing life in an 18th-century Provençal townhouse

facts.text: Each room is decorated with a historic French printed fabric, Indiennes and Toile de Jouy from the Braquenie workshops.
facts.excerpt: Each room is adorned with a historic French printed fabric — Indiennes and Toile de Jouy from the workshops of Braquenié, heirs to the Manufacture Royale de Jouy.

facts.text: Each Deluxe Room has its own colour palette inspired by the fabric chosen for its wall coverings.
facts.excerpt: Each Deluxe Room has its own distinctive colour palette, inspired by the fabric selected for its wall coverings.

facts.text: The bathrooms of the Grand Deluxe Rooms have built-in bathtubs of Arabescato Carrara marble.
facts.excerpt: In the bathrooms, "Belle Époque" elegance is expressed through built-in bathtubs crafted from "Arabescato" Carrara marble and Edwardian-inspired fittings

facts.text: The Suite is an 18th-century suite set between the gardens and the Palais des Papes.
facts.excerpt: An exceptional 18th-century suite, suspended between the gardens and the Palais des Papes, offering La Mirande’s most exclusive experience.

facts.text: Chef Michele Donvito, a native of Naples, took the helm at La Mirande in 2026.
facts.excerpt: In 2026, at the age of 32, he took the helm at La Mirande.

facts.text: At the gourmet restaurant the chef builds his menus as triptychs of three complementary dishes.
facts.excerpt: the chef crafts his menus as triptychs—three dishes that complement one another to tell a story

facts.text: The gourmet restaurant can be enjoyed in a Renaissance dining room or in a garden overlooking the Palais des Papes.
facts.excerpt: the splendor of a Renaissance dining room or the tranquility of a garden overlooking the Palais des Papes

facts.text: La Table Haute is the former Pamard family kitchen, with a 19th-century wood-fired stove, where up to twelve guests share a large sycamore table.
facts.excerpt: Equipped with a 19th-century wood-fired stove and surrounded by utensils that evoke the great culinary tradition, the historic kitchen welcomes up to twelve guests around its large sycamore wood table.

facts.text: At La Table Haute, Chef Thomas Longuesserre prepares a single menu for the whole table.
facts.excerpt: Here, Chef Thomas Longuesserre prepares a single menu for the entire table, inspired by the finest market finds and the seasonal produce of nearby farms.

facts.text: Bistrot Pamard is open seven days a week, with dining in the Louis XV salon or on the garden terrace facing the Palais des Papes.
facts.excerpt: perfect for lunch or dinner in the Louis XV salon beneath its Venetian chandeliers, or outdoors facing the Palais des Papes

facts.text: Le Mirage is a relaxed tavern whose name blends Mirande and garage.
facts.excerpt: The name is a playful portmanteau, blending _Mirande_ and _garage_

facts.text: Le Mirage serves regional wines by the carafe.
facts.excerpt: White, rosé and red wines from regional vineyards are served by the carafe.

facts.text: The bar pours signature creations with Chateauneuf-du-Pape wines and spirits from Avignon's Manguin Distillery.
facts.excerpt: signature creations showcasing the wines of Châteauneuf-du-Pape alongside spirits from Avignon's artisanal Manguin Distillery

facts.text: The garden, created by gardener Marc Leonetti, is cultivated according to the principles of organic farming.
facts.excerpt: Marc Leonetti, a gardener with a deep love of nature, has created an organised wilderness where box hedges, fruit trees, holm oaks, roses and aromatic herbs grow side by side

facts.text: The owners cultivate a four-hectare estate in Sarrians, in the Vaucluse, that supplies the kitchens with seasonal produce.
facts.excerpt: the owners cultivate an estate in Sarrians, in the Vaucluse — some twenty kilometres from the hotel — supplying the kitchens with seasonal produce

facts.text: The Chinese Cabinet is a Rococo room with Chinese wallpaper dating back to 1750.
facts.excerpt: Adorned with Chinese wallpaper dating back to 1750, this Rococo room reflects the 18th-century fascination with exoticism.

facts.text: The Cardinal's Room has a double-coffered Renaissance ceiling.
facts.excerpt: Dating back to the time of the Popes, the Cardinal’s Room features an impressive double-coffered Renaissance ceiling

facts.text: Concerts have always been held at La Mirande, as the owners are a music-loving family.
facts.excerpt: The owners being a music-loving family, there have always been concerts at La Mirande.

facts.text: Cooking classes with the chef can be taken in the former kitchen.
facts.excerpt: take part in a cooking class alongside him, in the heart of the former kitchen

facts.text: Pets are welcome for an additional charge.
facts.excerpt: Pets welcome (additional charge applies)

facts.text: Valet parking is available for an additional charge.
facts.excerpt: Valet parking (additional charge applies)

facts.text: The rooms have Tesla and universal charging stations.
facts.excerpt: Tesla and universal charging stations

facts.text: The Palais des Papes is the world's largest Gothic palace and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.excerpt: romantic views of the Palais des Papes, the world's largest Gothic palace and a UNESCO World Heritage Site

facts.text: The gourmet restaurant is open Thursday through Sunday.
facts.excerpt: Open Thursday through Sunday

facts.text: The Masquerade Ball on Saturday, November 14th 2026 requires an 18th-century costume.
facts.excerpt: **18th century costume mandatory**

facts.text: Bistrot Pamard has long been a favourite with locals and visitors.
facts.excerpt: Bistrot Pamard has long been a favourite dining destination for the people of Avignon and visitors alike.
